title: Ikea just took over your smart home
author: David Pierce

recommendations.name: Ikea Bilresa
recommendations.blurb: If anyone is going to really democratize the idea of the smart home, it’s Ikea. I am into most of the nearly two dozen Matter-compatible things the company announced this week, from lights to sensors to controllers, but the super customizable Bilresa buttons and remotes won me over immediately.

recommendations.name: Predator: Badlands
recommendations.blurb: Whenever a movie gets reviews that are like, “It’s well-made and a great time but it’s not exactly High Art,” I confess I immediately get excited. Give me more dumb fun! This appears to be a little dumb and a lot of fun. I’m in.

recommendations.name: Pluribus
recommendations.blurb: “Created by Vince Gilligan, the creator of Breaking Bad and Better Call Saul ” is literally all the pitch this show requires for me. But the fact that it’s a sci-fi show — about a world in which everyone is a little too happy — makes it even more exciting.

recommendations.name: Sora for Android
recommendations.blurb: The Sora hype continues! Honestly I’m getting tired of seeing AI-generated stuff all over my social feeds, but I keep hearing from folks who love making videos of themselves in all sorts of funny situations.

recommendations.name: Europa Universalis V
recommendations.blurb: I didn’t know anything about this game, or even this series, until this week. But a massive, world-conquering strategy game is extremely up my alley. I almost lost a lot of friends over Risk games… I wonder how this’ll go.

recommendations.name: Shuffalo
recommendations.blurb: A new daily game from The New Yorker in which you have to make progressively longer words with progressively more letters. Scratches my Bananagrams -loving brain so nicely.

recommendations.name: Niagara Launcher’s Artistic Update
recommendations.blurb: Niagara remains my favorite Android launcher, and I really like the direction this update takes the product: The team tapped a bunch of great artists to make not just cool wallpapers but whole themes that reimagine everything about your device. Also, the new dark icon pack? Gorgeous.

recommendations.name: BeeBot
recommendations.blurb: Super clever new app from Foursquare founder Dennis Crowley, which he refers to as “Waze meets Gossip Girl.” Basically, it’s an audio-only app that will pipe up in your headphones and periodically tell you about what’s happening nearby.

recommendations.name: WhatsApp for Apple Watch
recommendations.blurb: This, plus the recent iPad app, suggests to me that WhatsApp is really pushing hard to become your default messaging service across all devices and platforms. For me it’s mostly a group chat platform, but I’m pumped to be able to do tapback reactions from my wrist.

recommendations.name: Operation Space Station
recommendations.blurb: The first of this two-part PBS series on the International Space Station is, in a word, epic. I always figured building a city in space would be hard, and I had no idea. This is way more dramatic than any space movie.

recommendations.name: iPhone 16 Pro Max
recommendations.blurb: The phone: iPhone 16 Pro Max.

recommendations.name: Blank Spaces
recommendations.blurb: The apps: Blank Spaces.

recommendations.name: Dumb Phone
recommendations.blurb: We’ve talked about this launcher — and others like it, such as Dumb Phone — before, but it’s basically an iOS widget designed to replace your entire homescreen with big, text-based app launchers. (Fair warning: it costs $4 a month, or $24 lifetime.)

recommendations.name: King Sorrow
recommendations.blurb: Stephen King’s son wrote an 800 page book called King Sorrow that is (reductively) Millennial It. The title is a conjured dragon that embodies the very notion of evil. But it’s also a play on the author’s famous father, and his half-century of work. I’d say read it, but don’t do that: go audiobook!

recommendations.name: Today’s Budget
recommendations.blurb: I’ve been using Today’s Budget for the past month and it fundamentally changed how I view my finances. Created by just two people, the app answers a simple question that no other app can easily answer: How much can you actually spend today?

recommendations.name: n8n
recommendations.blurb: Hi! I’ve been exploring the n8n platform for automating (not only) tasks. I’ve built an automation which sends me D&B events everyday. I was pleasantly surprised how powerful n8n is!

recommendations.name: Affinity
recommendations.blurb: Affinity! Down with the Adobe monopoly.

recommendations.name: Dispatch
recommendations.blurb: I can recommend the game Dispatch, some described it as a game where you cannot fail. It’s similar to Telltale, where you choose the dialog and do some mini games. Reminds me of Black Mirror: Bandersnatch.

recommendations.name: Staccs
recommendations.blurb: Staccs is literally mind-bending. It’s a super lightweight matching card game (think Uno ) that has just enough complexity to keep every game interesting but still accessible enough for younger kids. But what sets Staccs apart is the visual design.

recommendations.name: Frank Prisinzano
recommendations.blurb: Anyone with even a passing interest in cooking needs to follow Frank Prisinzano (I follow on instagram but he’s all over). Start learning his methods (not recipes) and start changing your life!

recommendations.name: Pantheon
recommendations.blurb: If you haven’t watched Pantheon on Netflix, it’s worth it.

recommendations.name: Mac Studio
recommendations.blurb: I recently got a Mac Studio and set up Tailscale and Jellyfin to get access to all of my (legally obtained) media from anywhere across the world. Tailscale creates a direct and private VPN to your devices. Jellyfin is a much better open source alternative to Plex.
